author: William Ernest Henley
lines: Out of the night that covers me,
Black as the pit from pole to pole,
I thank whatever gods may be
For my unconquerable soul.
text: Out of the night that covers me,   Black as the pit from pole to pole, I thank whatever gods may be   For my unconquerable soul.
title: Invictus

author: William Ernest Henley
lines: In the fell clutch of circumstance
I have not winced nor cried aloud.
Under the bludgeonings of chance
My head is bloody, but unbowed.
text: In the fell clutch of circumstance   I have not winced nor cried aloud. Under the bludgeonings of chance   My head is bloody, but unbowed.
title: Invictus

author: William Ernest Henley
lines: Beyond this place of wrath and tears
Looms but the Horror of the shade,
And yet the menace of the years
Finds and shall find me unafraid.
text: Beyond this place of wrath and tears   Looms but the Horror of the shade, And yet the menace of the years   Finds and shall find me unafraid.
title: Invictus

author: William Ernest Henley
lines: It matters not how strait the gate,
How charged with punishments the scroll,
I am the master of my fate,
I am the captain of my soul.
text: It matters not how strait the gate,   How charged with punishments the scroll, I am the master of my fate,   I am the captain of my soul.
